items.title: Popular bakery and restaurant closed due to health violations in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga bakery/takeout spot has been forced to close following a failed health inspection. Revrea’s Grill & Bakeshop, located at 1057 Dundas St W, was inspected and shut down on Wednesday, Nov. 25. The restaurant specializes in authentic Filipino cuisine and baked goods. The report from Peel Public Health alleges that the restaurant did not use good housekeeping practices, and did not keep the premises free from any condition considered a health hazard. The restaurant is closed and may reopen after passing a follow-up inspection. This is the only red card on the restaurant’s public record, which shows inspections going back to June 2025. Red cards are issued when an inspector finds a health risk or danger, and the establishment or service is closed until the risks are removed. A yellow conditional pass means the establishment is not following all the requirements under the Health Protection and Promotion Act, and issues that pose a risk of illness must be corrected at the time of inspection. items.title: Slain police officer has bridge named for him in Mississauga
items.summary: A pedestrian bridge in Mississauga’s north end is being officially named in honour of a police officer who was killed while responding to a call in that part of the city more than 40 years ago. City of Mississauga officials said they’ll host a dedication ceremony on Dec. m. to officially mark the renaming of the Lake Wabukayne Pedestrian Bridge to the Constable Dwayne Piukkala Bridge. The pedestrian route crosses over Winston Churchill Boulevard, just north of Britannia Road West in Meadowvale, along Lake Wabukayne Trail. City councillors, Peel Regional Police, members of the Piukkala family and other community representatives will attend Tuesday’s ceremony to honour the slain Peel Regional Police officer. “The City of Mississauga is proud to honour the late Const. Piukkala by naming a bridge in his memory. His dedication to public service and commitment to the community continue to be remembered and celebrated,” city officials said in announcing details of the upcoming ceremony. “He is being recognized for his service, dedication and lasting contributions to the community. ” Peel Regional Police Const. items.title: Mississauga Council Seeks Judicial Review After AGCO Approves Cannabis Shop in Meadowvale Village
items.summary: According to Mississauga Ward 11 Coun. Brad Butt, city council voted after a closed session this week to pursue a judicial review of the AGCO's decision to grant a retail cannabis licence in the historic Meadowvale Village area. Butt told residents in a letter that staff will keep gathering information through the litigation and will raise concerns with the AGCO if eligibility rules were not met or errors occurred. He said a judicial review is not a new hearing on store approval, but asks the court to examine whether the AGCO's process was reasonable. Many residents have signed a petition against the shop, arguing it compromises the neighbourhood's historic character, and members of Protect Old Meadowvale Village demonstrated outside city hall this week. Opponents say the location is too close to schools and homes and allege the AGCO failed to properly consult them.

items.title: Princess Royal Drive Pipe Break Forces Shutdown of Mississauga City Hall and Nearby Buildings
items.summary: According to the Region of Peel, a significant watermain break on Princess Royal Drive in downtown Mississauga has shut off water to City Hall, the Living Arts Centre, the central library and other nearby municipal buildings. Crews have been on site since the evening of Nov. 26 assessing the damage and carrying out repairs, the region said in a statement. To complete the repairs safely, crews must isolate the affected section of the water main. The region said running water has also been temporarily shut off for nearby properties and buildings while the work continues. No timeline was given for when water service or building access would be restored.

items.title: House of the week: Indoor pool and 17 skylights features of this Mississauga home
items.summary: This place: This Lakeview home boasts 17 skylights, an indoor pool and four gas fireplaces. Features: This home offers over 4,200 square feet of total living space. Features include high ceilings, large windows, 17 remotely operated skylights, hardwood flooring, heated tile floors, custom millwork and four gas fireplaces. The custom kitchen showcases cabinetry, Miele appliances, granite countertops and a centre island with built-in refrigerators, a food warmer and a breakfast bar. A separate family room and upper-level library and office overlook the kitchen. A main-floor den/office could also be a guest bedroom. The primary bedroom has a cathedral ceiling, skylights, a gas fireplace, motorized shutters, a walk-in closet and an ensuite bathroom with a skylight and French doors. A second primary bedroom features a fireplace and an ensuite bathroom. There is another bedroom and a three-piece bathroom in the finished basement. The home has a 16-foot by 32-foot indoor pool, bar, sauna, hot tub and spa room with surround sound. The glass-enclosed pool area features a skylit ceiling, a dehumidification system, temperature-controlled heating and solar-assisted heating. Outside features include mature landscaping, a covered entertaining area, a built-in barbecue, and a private ravine setting backing onto the Etobicoke Creek. There are no rear neighbours.

items.title: Mississauga Truck Rollover on Hwy 401-410 Ramp: Your Injury Rights
items.summary: A transport truck rollover closed the ramp from westbound Highway 401 to northbound Highway 410 in Mississauga on Friday, November 27, 2026. Ontario Provincial Police warned drivers that the ramp would stay closed for most of the day. m. and was still there hours later. m. In a video posted online, Kerry Schmidt of the OPP described the truck's path. He said it travelled through the weeds, slid up an embankment, and then slid forward. He also said the truck's trailer buckled during the incident. Police reported minor injuries. However, they did not say who was hurt or whether anyone was taken to hospital. The OPP said the driver has been charged with careless driving under Ontario's traffic laws. A charge is not a finding of fault. The allegation has not been tested in court. items.title: One of Ontario's Biggest Supermarkets Opens on Matheson Boulevard in Mississauga
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Food World Plus has officially opened at 50 Matheson Blvd. E. near Eglinton Avenue and Hurontario Street, becoming one of the biggest supermarkets ever built in Ontario. The 176,000 square foot international mega market offers a wide selection of multicultural and specialty foods from East Asia, South Asia, Europe, the Mediterranean, the Caribbean and the Middle East. The store celebrated its grand opening on Oct. 30 and now operates daily, with longer hours on weekdays than on weekends. Departments include fresh produce, a butcher section with Certified Angus beef and halal meats, a seafood counter, a bakery, prepared foods, sushi, pizza and gelato. The outlet describes the store as a destination for shoppers seeking international foods and specialty ingredients from around the world.

items.title: Water service back in downtown Mississauga following repairs to water main break
items.summary: A water main break in downtown Mississauga that shut down city hall, the Living Arts Centre and Hazel McCallion Central Library on Friday has been repaired, Peel Region officials said early Friday afternoon.

items.title: Mayor Tedjo Vows to Defend Mississauga's Data Centre Freeze as Two Firms Appeal to Land Tribunal
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, two real estate firms have filed appeals with the Ontario Land Tribunal against the city's one-year freeze on large-scale data centre developments. The appeals come from U.S.-based industrial real estate firm Prologis and Toronto-based Montcrest Asset Management, both challenging the interim control bylaw that took effect Sept. 16. The bylaw bars new or expanded data centres with a peak power demand of 10 megawatts or more while staff review planning and zoning rules. Prologis, which had submitted a development application for a proposed data centre near Tenth Line West in Meadowvale Business Park, filed its appeal on Nov. 4. Speaking to reporters after council's inaugural meeting on Nov. 16, Mayor Alvin Tedjo said the city is prepared to defend its bylaw at the tribunal. The city has also launched a public engagement review on data centre impacts.

items.title: 34th Shoppers Drug Mart Location Opens Near Square One in Mississauga
items.summary: According to a Shoppers news release, a new Shoppers Drug Mart opened Friday morning at 175 Burnhamthorpe Rd. W., east of Duke of York Boulevard near Square One, marking the chain's 34th location in Mississauga. The new store offers a range of health, beauty and postal services. At the centre of the location is a dedicated Pharmacy Care Clinic, designed to help patients access healthcare services closer to home, the release said. The beauty department features a selection of international and specialty skincare brands. The store also includes a Canada Post office.
